===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|iland|yland||obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|ylond|ylelond||obsolete}}<!-- These look rather like Middle English -->

===Etymology===
{{word|en|ine|h₂ékʷeh₂}}
{{etymon|en|iland|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*lendʰ-|id=land}}
From earlier {{m|en|iland}}, from {{inh|en|enm|iland}}, {{m|enm|yland}}, {{m|enm|ylond}}, from {{inh|en|ang|īeġland}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*auwjuland}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*awjōlandą}} (from {{der|en|gem-pro|*awjō|t=island, waterland, meadow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₂ekʷeh₂}}) + {{m|gem-pro|*landą|t=land}}, equivalent to {{af|en|ey|id1=island|land}}.

{{doublet|en|Öland}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|island}}, {{m|sco|iland}}, {{m|sco|yland||island}}, {{cog|fy|eilân||island}}, {{cog|stq|Ailound||island}}, {{cog|nl|eiland||island}}, {{cog|nds|Eiland||island}}, {{cog|de|Eiland||island}}, {{cog|sv|ö||island}}, {{m|sv|Öland||Sweden's second largest island}}, {{cog|da|ø||island}}, {{cog|no|øy||island}}, {{m|no|øyland||large island}}, {{cog|is|eyland||island}}.

The insertion of ⟨s⟩—a 16th century spelling modification—is due to a change in spelling to the unrelated term {{m|en|isle}}, which previously lacked ''s'' (cf. {{noncog|enm|ile}}, {{m|enm|yle}}). The re-addition was mistakenly carried over to include ''iland'' as well. Related also to {{cog|de|Aue||water-meadow}}, {{cog|la|aqua||water}}. More at {{l|en|ea}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[contiguous]] [[area]] of [[land]], smaller than a [[continent]], totally [[surround]]ed by [[water]].
#* {{RQ:Donne Devotions|chapter=17. Meditation|pages=415–416|pageref=415|passage=No man is an '''''Iland''''', intire of it ſelfe; euery man is a peece of the ''Continent'', a part of the ''maine''; {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1975|title={{w|Jaws (film)|Jaws}}|writers=w:Peter Benchley; w:Carl Gottlieb|role=Brody|actor=Roy Scheider|passage=It's only an '''island''' if you look at it from the water…}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Gordon L. Rottman|title=World War 2 Pacific island guide|passage=Sumatra is the second largest '''island''' in the East Indies and the fourth largest in the world covering 182,859 square miles.}}
# {{lb|en|by extension|in place names}} A [[contiguous]] [[area]] of [[land]], smaller than a [[continent]], partially [[surround]]ed by [[water]]; a [[peninsula]]; a [[half-island]].
#: {{ux|en|Despite its name, Barry '''Island''' is actually a peninsula}}
# An [[entity]] [[surround]]ed by other entities that are very [[different]] from itself.
#: {{ux|en|The quiet library was an '''island''' of tranquility in the noisy, bustling city.}}
#: {{ux|en|an '''island''' of colors on a butterfly's wing}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Daniel Taylor|title=Liverpool go through after Mohamed Salah stops Manchester City fightback|work={{w|The Guardian}} (London)|date=10 April 2018|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/apr/10/manchester-city-liverpool-champions-league-match-report
|passage= He was on the ball in a flash, swerving to the left of City’s goalkeeper, Ederson, before shaping his body for a tricky angled finish. He was an '''island''' of composure, floating in his 39th goal of the season with a delicate chip into the corner.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261012140613/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/apr/10/manchester-city-liverpool-champions-league-match-report|archivedate=12 October 2026}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=October 27 1939|author=Deseret News|journal=Roosevelt Reaffirms American Neutrality
|passage=King Leopold, speaking in fluent English during his six minute broadcast, said Belgium stood side by side with Holland "an '''Island''' of peace in the interests of all"}}
# A [[superstructure]] on an [[aircraft carrier]]'s [[deck]].
# A [[traffic island]].
#: {{ux|en|the '''island''' in the middle of a roundabout}}
# {{lb|en|by extension|West Midlands}} A [[roundabout]]; a [[traffic circle]].
#: {{ux|en|Dunton '''island''', near Birmingham, is one of the most confusingly labelled '''islands''' in the U.K.}}
#: {{ux|en|In Coventry, you will often hear people say: “Turn right at the '''island'''”.}}
# A bench, counter, etc., that is not connected to a wall or other furniture and which can be used from any side.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1936|author=w:F.J. Thwaites|title={{w|The Redemption (novel)|The Redemption}}|publisher=H. John Edwards|location=Sydney|year_published=1940|chapter=XXII|page=216|text=A short, rather studious young woman on noticing him moved from behind an '''island''' counter.}}
## {{lb|en|by extension}} {{ellipsis of|en|kitchen island}}.
# {{lb|en|government}} An [[unincorporated]] area wholly surrounded by one or more incorporated areas.
# {{lb|en|grammar}} A [[phrase]] from which a [[wh-word]] cannot be [[extract]]ed without yielding invalid grammar.
#: {{ux|en|Adverbial subordinate clauses are '''islands''' for extraction: "They have a billion dollars of inventory that they don't know where *(it) is".}}

=====Usage notes=====
* As with the names of {{m|en|[[river]]s}}, {{m|en|[[mount]]s}} and {{m|en|[[mountain]]s}}, the names of lakes are typically formed by adding the word before or after the unique term: {{m|en|Lake Titicaca}} or {{m|en|Great Slave Lake}}. Generally speaking, names formed using adjectives or attributives see {{m|en||lake}} added to the end, as with {{m|en|Reindeer Lake}}; {{m|en||lake}} is usually added before proper names, as with {{m|en|Lake Michigan}}. This derives from the earlier but now uncommon form {{m|en||lake of ~}}: for instance, the 19th-century {{m|en|Lake of Annecy}} is now usually simply {{m|en|Lake Annecy}}. There are exceptions to this generalization, however, including notably the names of the individual [[Finger Lakes]] (e.g. [[Oneida]] Lake, [[Seneca]] Lake, [[Cayuga]] Lake). It frequently occurs, however, that foreign placenames are misunderstood as proper nouns, as with the Chinese {{m|en|Taihu||Great Lake}} and {{m|en|Qinghai||Blue Sea}} being frequently rendered as {{m|en|Lake Tai}} and {{m|en|Qinghai Lake}}.
